description_en: Located in Konti (Kumbheshwar) Ṭola of Patan, Kontī Bahī is one of the 15 majorbahīsof Lalitpur. The classical name of Konti Bahī is Kāśyapamiśrasaṃskārita Lalitavarṇamahāvihāra, which suggests that a person named Kāśyapa Miśra either established or restored thebahī.Eleven stone steps lead to the courtyard, and upon entering, one can see dilapidated wooden statues of Mahākāla and Lokeśvara in a niche to the north. A stonedharmacakrais placed at the bottom of the Mahākāla statue, and a sculpture of a lotus flower and avajracan be found to its right and left, respectively. Art historians consider thedharmacakrato be from the Licchavi period (Pal1974, plates 162, 163;Bangdel1995, 247).The two-storey esoteric god-house of thebahīfaces east. Its roof is tiled withjhĩgaṭīand topped with a stone pinnacle. Mostbahīhave aphucāon top of their roof, however, this feature is absent here. Thebahībuildings were severely damaged in the 2015 earthquake. The single storey building was constructed after the earlier cracked building at the northern corner was dismanted. In the first half of 2020, the southern building remained under construction, while the restoration process of the eastern building had not yet begun. A historical photo of the monument shows that there was once a veranda on the first floor of the buildings. A Licchavi periodAśokacaityais located in the courtyard of thebahī.The esoteric deity of thebahīis located on the first floor in the esoteric god house (āgamachẽ). A historical photo of the building shows atoraṇafixed on the veranda in front of theāgamaroom, however, it is now missing. The sanctum of thebahīis on the ground floor, and houses a statue of Buddha inbhaviṣyavyākaraṇaposture. The statue shows Śākyamuni Buddha in a form which will be adopted by the future Buddha, Maitreya. Previously, a similar statue made of clay and gold clad was enshrined here, but this was stolen in 2001. The lower part of this statue of Buddha’s leg broke off during the theft and has been preserved in the sanctum. A circumambulatory path surrounds the sanctum.TheNepālikabhūpavaṃśāvalī(12.7-37) chronicle mentions the establishment of thebahī. It states that a Brahmin named Sunayaśrī Miśra from Kapilabastu arrived in Patan and lived near Kumbheśvara. In search of a spiritual guru, he went to Lhāsā, where he learned fromlāmas. Afterwards, he returned to Nepal, where he presented a crystal jewel to King Rudradeva. The King offered him land near the Aśoka Caitya, and he built a monastic building there. Later, Sunayaśrī, Govardhana Miśra and Kāśyapa Miśra came to Patan from Kapilavastu in search of their guru. Both of them settled in Patan, where they established two monasteries named Dunta and Lalivana respectively. Not having heard any news from Sunayaśrī Miśra, his wife and son too came to Patan in search of him. The family was reunited, and Sunayaśrī built them a house called Chokā near hisvihāra. When a grandson was born, Sunayaśrī made him abhikṣu. He also dictated that any sons of his descendants must leave their homes and live a life of celibacy in thevihāra. Sunayaśrī’svihārais now called Yampi Bahī (LAL1550), and those of his disciples are called Konti Vihāra and Pintu Bahī (LAL0970).The oldest inscription of the Bahī is dated NS 743. If one considers the Licchavi Dharmacakra, Aśoka Caitya and the story of the chronicle, it seems likely that the Bahī was established in the Licchavi period.Only two families are associated with the Bahī. Of the two, Sanukaji Shakya’s family has been conducting daily worships and taking care of the Bahī. With the exception of the daily worship, all religious activities such as feasts for thesaṅghamembers, the worship of Mahākāla, and the annual ritual worship of thecaityahave come to an end.
description_ne: ललितपुरका प्रमुख १५ वटा बहीहरूमध्ये कोन्ति बही पनि एउटा हो । कोन्ति (कुम्भेश्वर) टोलमा बनाइएको बही हुनाले जनभाषामा यसलाई कोन्ति बही भनिएको हो । संस्कृतमा यस बहीलाई काश्यपमिश्रसंस्कारित ललितवर्णमहाविहार भनिन्छ । कोन्ति टोलको प्राचीन नाम ललितवन हो । काश्यप मिश्र नाम गरेको व्यक्तिले ललितवन भएको क्षेत्रमा बनाएको बही हुनाले काश्यप मिश्र संस्कारित ललितवर्ण महाविहार नाम रहेको हो । बहीभित्र पुग्न ११ तहको ढुंगाको सिँढी चढेर जानुपर्छ । बहीको प्रवेशद्वारबाट भित्र पसेपछि उत्तरमा महाकाल र लोकेश्वरको काठको अत्यन्त जीर्ण मूर्ति राखिएको देखिन्छ । त्यसको मुनि ढुंगाको धर्मचक्र कुँदिएको छ । धर्मचक्रको दायाँबायाँ कमलको फूल र वज्र कुँदिएको छ । कलाविद्‌हरूले यसलाई लिच्छविकालको मानेका छन् । बहीको द्य:छेँ पूर्वाभिमुख गरी दुई तलाको रहेको छ । छानामा झिँगटी राखी ढुंगाको चैत्यलाई गजूर बनाई स्थापना गरिएको छ । बहीको छानामा पुल (फुचा) हुनुपर्नेमा यहाँ त्यस्तो बनाइएको छैन । पहिले बहीको चारैतिर बार्दली निकालिएको भए पनि विसं २०७२ को भूकम्पले क्षति पुगेपछि उत्तरतर्फको भागलाई भत्काएर एक तला मात्र बनाइएको छ । दक्षिणतिरको भागको पुनर्निर्माणको काम हुँदैछ भने पूर्वतर्फको भाग पनि पूरै भत्किएको अवस्था छ । द्य:छेँको पहिलो तलामा बहीको आगम राखिएको छ । पहिलो तलाको बार्दलीमा पहिले तोरण राखिएको थियो तर अहिले उक्त तोरण देखिँदैन । भुइँतलामा बहीको गन्धकुटी रहेको छ । गन्धकुटीको चारैतिर प्रदक्षिणा गर्न मिल्ने गरी प्रदक्षिणापथ बनाइएको छ । गन्धकुटीमा प्रवेश गर्ने ढोका साधारण किसिमले बनाइएको छ । गन्धकुटीतिर जाने सिँढीको दायाँबायाँ एक जोडी ढुंगाको सिंह स्थापना गरिएको छ । गर्भगृहभित्र पूर्वाभिमुख गरी भविष्यव्याकरण मुद्रामा रहेका बुद्धलाई गन्धुरी देवताको रूपमा स्थापना गरिएको छ । गन्धुरी देवताको पुरानो मूर्ति माटोले बनेको थियो र सुनको मोलम्बा लगाइएको तामाको पाताले मोडिएको थियो । विसं २०५८ सालमा पुरानो मूर्ति चोरी भएपछि अहिले माटोकै नयाँ मूर्ति बनाएर स्थापना गरिएको छ । चोरहरूले मूर्ति उखेल्दा उछिट्टिएको खुट्टा पनि गन्धकुटीभित्रै सुरक्षितपूर्वक राखिएको छ । तेलिया इँटा छापिएको बही प्राङ्गणमा एउटा लिच्छविकालीन अशोक चैत्य स्थापना गरिएको छ ।यो बहीको निर्माणसम्बन्धी कुनै लिखित अभिलेख प्राप्त भएको छैन । नेपालिकभूपवंशावली(१२.७-३७)मा सुनयश्री मिश्रसँग जोडेर यो बहीको स्थापनाबारे लेखिएको छ । वंशावलीमा लेखिएअनुसार राजा रुद्रदेवको पालामा कपिलवस्तुबाट आएका सुनयश्री मिश्रले यम्पि महाविहार (LAL1550) बनाएर त्यहीँ बसोबास गरिरहेका थिए । धेरै समयसम्म पनि गुरु नफर्केपछि उनका शिष्यहरू गोवर्द्धन मिश्र र काश्यप मिश्र उनलाई खोज्दै ललितपुरमा आइपुगे । गुरु सुनयश्री मिश्रले दुबै शिष्यहरूको लागि एक‍-एकवटा विहार बनाइदिए जसलाई दुन्तु विहार र ललितवन विहार भनिन्छ । उता आफ्नो श्रीमान् फर्केर नआएपछि सुनयश्री मिश्रकी श्रीमती पनि श्रीमान् खोज्दै ललितपुर आएर बसिन् । पछि सुनयश्री मिश्रको छोराको पनि छोरा जन्मिएपछि सुनयश्री मिश्रले आफ्नो छोरालाई भिक्षु बनाइदिए । त्यसपछि सुनयश्री मिश्रले आफ्ना अनुयायीहरूलाई छोरा जन्मिएपछि गृहस्थी जीवन त्यागेर ब्रम्हचर्य जीवन बिताउनुपर्ने नियम बनाइदिए । सुनयश्री मिश्रको विहारलाई यम्पि विहार भन्न थालियो भने उनका शिष्यहरूमध्ये काश्यप मिश्रको लागि बनाइएको विहारलाई क्वन्ति विहार भन्न थालियो (Nepālikabhūpavaṃśāvalī2016, 12.7-37) । बहीमा लिच्छविकालको धर्मचक्र कुँदिएको कलात्मक ढुंगा स्थापना गरिएको हुनाले लिच्छविकालमै यो बही स्थापना भइसकेको तर्क गर्न सकिन्छ । यहाँ पाइएका अभिलेखमध्ये सबभन्दा पुरानो अभिलेख नेसं ७४३ को ताम्रपत्र हो ।यस बहीमा दुईवटा मात्र परिवार आबद्ध रहेका छन् । ती दुईमध्ये सानुकाजी शाक्यको एउटा परिवारले मात्र बहीको रेखदेख गर्नेदेखि लिएर नित्यपूजा संचालन गरिरहेको छ । यहाँ नित्यपूजा बाहेक संघभोजन, महाकाल पूजा, चैत्यको वर्षबन्धन जस्ता धार्मिक क्रियाकलापहरू बन्द भइसकेका छन् ।
brick_type: mā apā (regular fired brick), dāci apā (conical veneer brick)
references: Sources and references Sources Local knowledge: Member of saṅgha, Śākya, male, age 46

historical_events.event_description: Thieves stole the clay and gold idol of Buddha. They took out the gilded plates and left the clay part on the road. The clay was found four days after the theft. After some time, a new idol was made by carrying new clay from Mhepi of Kathmandu and mixing it with the old clay.

During the reign of King Siddhinarasingh Malla, the chief monk of the Bahī (Thapaḥju) offered a goldenkalaśato the main deity of the Bahī. Mukundarāja Bhāro, Jivasaṃkha Bhāro, Viṣṇuśrī Kalyāṇa and Vitu Siṃha were given the responsibility of caring for it.

During the reign of King Yoganrendra Malla, Bhāṇi Siṃha, Kṛṣṇasiṃha Bhāvo, Harisiṃha Bhāvo, Kalyāṇasiṃha Bhāvo and Maṇirāma Bhāvo pavedteliyābricks in the sanctum. At that time the chief monk of the Bahī was Dhanadeva.

historical_events.event_name: Construction of pavement in the bahī courtyard
historical_events.event_description: Minister Kisnarāma Bhāro, Dharmmarāma Bhāvo, Maṇirāma Bhāvo and Kamalasiṅ Bhāvo made a plinth in the Bahī.

historical_events.event_name: Pavement with teliyābrick at the bahī courtyard
historical_events.event_description: A group including Śrīju Bhikṣu, Śaṃkhamura Bhāvo, Dhaneśvara, Parisiṃ and others paved the courtyard withteliyābricks.
The 1934 earthquakes destroyed most of the Bahī. Later thesaṅgha-members of the Bahī restored it.

historical_events.event_name: Construction of Mañjuśrī Pādukā and Caitya
historical_events.event_description: Bekhāratna Khaḍgī established Mañjuśrī Pādukā (LAL0101-007) and the Caitya (LAL0101-008) in the Bahī.
After the old idol was stolen, Sanukaji Shakya made a new clay idol and installed it at his own expense.

historical_events.event_name: Reconstruction of the esoteric god house
historical_events.event_description: The esoteric god house (dyaḥchẽ) of the Bahī was dilapidated and so rebuilt with the financial support of the Lalitpur Sub-Metropolitan Municipality. The locals bore 15 per cent of the cost and the Municipality took on 85 per cent of the cost.
The 2015 earthquakes damaged the eastern, southern and northern parts of Bahī. Later, the upper floors of the damaged houses were demolished.

historical_events.event_name: Reconstruction of southern part of bahī
historical_events.event_description: The monument is under reconstruction. Province No. 3 (Bagmati Province) provided 5 million rupees for the first phase of reconstruction. The reconstruction work on the southern part of the Bahī is still ongoing (2020).
Dharmarāja and Aindrarāja erected a statue of Amitābha Buddha in memory of Dharmadeva Bhikṣu.
